source: PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents
summary: Supervisor-worker harness for live self-improvement: a supervisor can redirect or abort the active worker during execution, and distills failure modes revealed mid-run into reusable skills. 14.6-point improvement on Terminal-Bench 2.0 with 42.9% fewer tokens per task.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — the live steering and skill-distillation-during-run concepts map directly to HID-186 (partial retry) and HID-188 (episodic memory), but both those themes are already tracked as open issues. Would strengthen existing issues rather than warrant a new one.

summary: Autonomous ML experimentation loop released March 2026: coding agent proposes changes, runs a short training job, commits improvements, rolls back regressions. 66k+ stars, 700 experiments in 2 days discovering 20 optimizations.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — targets ML research experimentation loops (eval → commit/rollback), not software issue orchestration. AgentForge's pipeline already has plan-review and AI-review gating; the commit/rollback model doesn't map cleanly to the Linear state machine.

summary: CrewAI stable release 1.14.3 (April 2026) adds runtime state checkpointing backed by Qdrant Edge; crossed 450M agentic workflows/month with FedRAMP and SSO support.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — checkpointing aligns with the partial-retry theme (HID-186), which is already tracked as an open issue. No new capability gap surfaces.

summary: GA April 2026: YAML agent definitions, graph-based workflows with checkpointing, native MCP and A2A protocol support. Replaces AutoGen which entered maintenance mode in Oct 2025.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — A2A protocol support is novel but AgentForge uses CLI subprocesses not API agents; no verified gap for inter-agent protocol in current architecture. Graph-based checkpointing overlaps HID-186.

source: E-mem: Multi-Agent Based Episodic Context Reconstruction for LLM Agent Memory
summary: Multi-agent episodic context reconstruction with multi-scope identity tagging (user_id, agent_id, run_id); shows only marginal degradation under cross-session noise where standard RAG experiences severe drops.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly relevant to cross-run episodic memory, but this theme is already tracked by HID-188 (inject cross-run episodic memory). No new issue warranted.

source: RaMem: Contextual Reinstatement for Long-term Agentic Memory
summary: Contextual reinstatement approach for long-term agentic memory; retrieves memory by reinstating the context in which an episode occurred rather than keyword/vector search alone.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — episodic memory theme already tracked by HID-188. The reinstatement retrieval technique could enrich that implementation, but not a separate gap.

summary: Framework for recursive decomposition and reasoning in agentic settings; agents spawn sub-agents with narrower scopes and merge results back up the call stack.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge deliberately uses sequential single-agent-per-stage execution. Recursive/hierarchical spawning conflicts with the explicit state machine design principle; rejected as speculative architecture.

summary: Google's agentic orchestration library (trending September 2026, 1,373 stars). Infrastructure-level agent coordination runtime targeting cloud-native deployment.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — cloud-native API-based orchestration doesn't align with AgentForge's CLI subprocess model. Not a feasible adoption path within 1-2 agent runs.
